items.stem: Which TWO observations are direct evidence that light behaves as a wave? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A double-slit experiment produces an interference pattern of bright and dark fringes
options.rationale: Correct: interference is a wave phenomenon.

options.text: A diffraction grating spreads white light into a spectrum
options.rationale: Correct: diffraction demonstrates the wave nature of light.

options.text: The photoelectric effect ejects electrons above a threshold frequency
options.rationale: The photoelectric effect is evidence for the particle (photon) nature of light.

options.text: Light travels in straight lines through a uniform medium
options.rationale: Rectilinear propagation is consistent with both ray and wave models and is not distinctive evidence.

items.explanation: Correct: interference is a wave phenomenon.

items.stem: An object is placed beyond the focal point of a converging lens. The image formed is

options.text: real, inverted and on the opposite side of the lens
options.rationale: Correct: an object outside the focal length of a converging lens forms a real, inverted image.
That occurs only when the object is inside the focal length.

options.text: virtual and on the same side as the object
options.rationale: A real image forms on the opposite side for this geometry.
An image at infinity requires the object at the focal point.

items.explanation: Correct: an object outside the focal length of a converging lens forms a real, inverted image.
